findings.plain_summary: OPM has finalized a rule that removes the governmentwide 52-week time-in-grade requirement for promotions to covered competitive-service General Schedule positions at GS-6 and above, effective January 14, 2027. Agencies may still impose their own job-related prerequisites, including a required period of service in grade, through written merit-promotion plans, and the rule also makes unspecified related changes to student appointment, training, and other personnel regulations.

items.headline: Agencies can still impose a time-in-grade requirement on their own through merit-promotion plans
items.what_changes: The governmentwide 52-week requirement goes away, but each agency may set a required period of service in grade as a promotion prerequisite in its written merit-promotion plan, as long as the requirement is applied consistently. Waiting periods could therefore persist agency by agency. The summary mentions 'job-related requirements' but does not say these can include time in grade.
items.speaker: OPM
items.quote: Agencies may continue to establish job-related promotion prerequisites, including a period of service in grade, through their written merit-promotion plans, provided those requirements are consistently applied.

items.headline: Effective date is January 14, 2027
items.what_changes: The time-in-grade restriction stays in force until January 14, 2027, nearly three months after the announcement. The summary does not give the date.
items.speaker: OPM

items.headline: Rule also changes regulations on student appointments, training, and other personnel matters
items.what_changes: Beyond time-in-grade, the final rule amends other personnel regulations, including student appointments and training. The release does not describe these changes, and the summary does not mention them.
items.speaker: OPM
items.quote: It also makes related changes to regulations governing student appointments, training, and other personnel matters.

items.headline: No guaranteed promotions; qualification standards and competitive procedures unchanged
items.what_changes: Removing the waiting period does not entitle anyone to a promotion. Qualification standards still apply, and agencies' competitive evaluation and selection procedures are unchanged.
items.speaker: OPM
items.quote: It does not guarantee a promotion, waive qualification standards, or change the competitive procedures agencies use to evaluate and select candidates.

items.headline: Scope limited to competitive-service GS positions at GS-6 and above
items.what_changes: The removal covers advancement to covered competitive-service General Schedule positions at GS-6 and above. The restriction it removes generally required 52 weeks at a lower grade.
items.speaker: OPM
items.quote: The US Office of Personnel Management (OPM) has finalized a rule removing the governmentwide time-in-grade restriction for advancement to covered competitive-service General Schedule positions at GS-6 and above.

items.headline: Change tied to early-career recruitment efforts
items.what_changes: OPM links the rule to making federal service more competitive for early-career talent. It cites the Early Careers Initiative and U.S. Tech Force.
items.speaker: OPM
items.quote: OPM said eliminating the governmentwide waiting period supports its effort to make federal service more competitive for early-career talent.

could_not_determine: How many employees or positions the change affects.
The specific CFR sections amended or removed, and the Federal Register citation for the final rule.
What the 'related changes' to student appointments, training, and other personnel matters actually do.
The number of public comments received, what commenters argued, and what OPM declined to change.
How the rule treats positions below GS-6, non-GS pay systems, or the excepted service.
Whether OPM will provide guidance or oversight on agencies that reinstate time-in-grade requirements through merit-promotion plans, or what 'consistently applied' requires in practice.

doc.title: OPM Finalizes Rule Removing Governmentwide Time-in-Grade Barrier to Promotions
